text:
mara: FYI - found a json-mode regression in py-sdk: optional fields become null after an auth-retry. sample app 'data-exporter' started failing.

jen: can you show a tiny repro?

mara: short one:
```py
# client.call_tool('export', {'format':'csv'})  # no 'limit'
# trigger auth refresh -> retry
# server receives: {'format':'csv', 'limit': None}
```

oscar: oh right. that breaks strict schemas where optional != nullable.

paul: looks like auth wrapper shallow-merges defaults into args before queuing for retry, turning missing keys into None. json.dumps then becomes null.

mara: i prototyped a sentinel (_UNSET) so we can preserve absence during retry; at send-time we treat UNSET as omit. works locally.

ci-bot: samples/data-exporter e2e failing: toolcall-optional-null.test.py

jen: add unit tests for (absent, None, value) across py-sdk jsonmode + auth refresh. also add an integration that flips the token mid-request.

oscar: ensure streaming reassembly path also respects UNSET; chunks sometimes materialize metadata keys.

paul: changelog note: "fix(python-sdk): preserve absent optional fields on auth/retry in JSON mode". create issue for backport.

mara: opened PR #4120 with sentinel impl and tests; left reproduction script in comments. will run canary once merged.

sdk-team: ack, reviewing. plan backport to 1.3.x if approved.

jen: also updated sample assertion expecting None -> removed to reflect strict optional semantics. will add migration note in release doc.

mara: thanks - keeping this thread for coordination. ping me for netem script.
